title: Add another sign-in factor
summary: Multi-factor authentication asks for more than one kind of proof. A security key or an authenticator can add protection beyond a password.
introduction: Multi-factor authentication asks for more than one kind of proof. A security key or an authenticator can add protection beyond a password. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Multi-factor authentication asks for more than one kind of proof. A security key or an authenticator can add protection beyond a password.

blocks.code:
Something you know: password
Something you have: security key
Two factors protect one sign-in
blocks.title: Add another sign-in factor

blocks.text: Two passwords are still both things you know. Different kinds of proof are what make multiple factors.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Identify the factor type of a physical security key.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Never share a one-time code with someone who contacts you unexpectedly.
For more detail later, use this [Cybersecurity Fundamentals further reading](https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world).
